Ford Racing Parts M-9000-PM52DCT Gets You a Predator Supercharged V8 and a Tremec DCT
46 photos
Photo: Tremec on Instagram
The rowdy 5.2-liter Predator V8 costs a massive $30,500 in crate engine format as of November 2026. Ford Racing Parts M-6007-M52SCA is described as the F-150 Raptor R specification of the supercharged lump, even though the half-ton pickup develops 720 ponies. But alas, Ford Racing Parts doesn't offer any transmission for this crate engine. That will change in the first quarter of 2027, all thanks to the folks at Tremec.
M-9000-PM52DCT is the part number under which FRP advertises the crate engine and tranny combo, which includes the M-6007-M52SCA mentioned earlier, 760 horsepower and all. M-9000-PM52DCT adds the dual-clutch box of the Mustang Dark Horse SC, along with all relevant wiring harnesses and controllers.
Tremec broke the news through social media, but alas, pricing has yet to be finalized. Tremec labels the package as the 5.2L DCT Supercharged Power Module, and just like the Raptor R specification, the crate engine in question develops 625 pound-feet (847 Newton-meters) if you give it premium gasoline.
As you're well aware, that's 35 horsepower and 35 pound-feet below the official figures of the Dark Horse SC. A beefy Eaton supercharger is the secret sauce here, complete with a 92-millimeter throttle body. The Predator's engine block uses high-strength aluminum and plasma-transferred wire arc spray-welded cylinder liners, a thermal spray coating that bonds a microscopic layer of molten steel to the aluminum bores.
The specs sheet provided by Tremec on Instagram also reveals a 94-millimeter bore and 93 millimeters of stroke, a 9.5:1 compression ratio, forged conrods, a forged crankshaft, and Grafal-coated forged aluminum pistons. Based on the aforementioned information, the novelty here is the addition of a dual-clutch tranny and the supporting electronics in a complete package.
Photo: Tremec on Instagram TR-9070 DCT is what Tremec calls the wet-clutch box in question, a tranny Ford previously used in the S550-generation Mustang Shelby GT500. For the S650-generation Mustang Dark Horse SC, both parties updated the control logic for smoother track consistency and faster response. The latest version of the 9070 works alongside next-gen MagneRide damping and Variable Traction Control for a more fulfilling driving experience.
Under specific conditions, the transmission in the Dark Horse SC delays upshifts to hit the engine's redline more precisely. Ford and Tremec also updated the housing to accommodate the S650 platform's packaging requirements, all while upgrading the cooling system for sustained track and drag strip duties. Both the GT500 and the SC pride themselves on a 3.73 Torsen limited-slip differential and carbon-fiber driveshaft.
While a manual transmission may cater to enthusiasts, a properly integrated twin-clutch design performs much better when you're racing against the clock. If you ask me, the 10R-series automatic would have been perfectly so as well, as demonstrated by the F-150 Raptor R.
Just like the standalone crate engine, this combo is restricted to competition and off-highway use. It's technically illegal to swap a non-certified or mismatched engine into a model year 1976 or newer vehicle. Pretty much anything from 1975 or earlier is generally exempt from these strict federal motor vehicle emissions compliance rules.
